Why airflow matters
−20% airflow
≈ −49% fan power
Fan power ≈ airflow³ (fan affinity laws, ideal case). Small airflow cuts, big energy savings.
Operational efficiency
Air change rates haven’t been reviewed since commissioning.
Fans run at full speed overnight and at weekends.
Sustainability & carbon
We don’t know what share of site energy our cleanrooms use.
Our carbon targets leave GMP areas out of scope.
Digitalisation & data
Particle data is logged for compliance, never used to control airflow.
We can’t see energy use per room or suite.
Compliance
Energy projects stall because nobody’s sure how QA will react.
Energy measures aren’t part of our Contamination Control Strategy.
Future-ready design
Our next build or refit is designed around fixed, worst-case airflow.
Our BMS can’t adjust airflow to live room conditions.

Three checks for next week

Back on site? Start here.

1

Check the headroom

Pull a month of particle monitoring data. If counts sit well below grade limits, at rest and in operation, you’re likely moving more air than you need.

2

Check the night shift

Do fans step down when rooms are empty? A validated setback mode is often the fastest, lowest-risk win.

3

Check in with QA

Assess each measure against your Contamination Control Strategy, like any other GMP change. Savings and compliance get signed off together.
